title: When Processing Email Stands for Productivity
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership criticizes organizations that treat email processing as productive work. The post argues that clearing an inbox delivers a dopamine hit and a sense of responsiveness, but it should not be mistaken for the real acts of leadership: coaching, giving feedback and building relationships. Good leaders set aside bounded time for email and spend most of their day making people and situations better. Practical suggestions include boundaries on checking and using filters and templates. The post ends with the claim that how a leader spends time defines the leader.
points: Some organizations count a day spent clearing the inbox as productive, which confuses activity with leadership.
Inbox zero gives a sense of accomplishment and a shot of dopamine, which is why the trap persists.
Good leaders choose coaching, feedback and relationship building over email busywork.
Boundaries on when to check email, plus filters and templates, help contain overload.
How a leader spends time defines who they are as a leader.
quotes: When processing email is considered as valuable as addressing issues, making decisions, and coaching others to success, leaders and team members feel self-satisfied by spending their time reading and responding to email.
No doubt clearing the inbox gives leaders a sense of accomplishment and a shot of dopamine. It feels fabulous to have wiped the inbox clean.

If given the choice between acts of leadership (such as coaching others, offering critical feedback in meetings, and building relationships) and processing email, good leaders choose leadership, not busywork.
They set aside time to process emails, but spend the majority of their time making situations and people better.
But setting boundaries regarding when to check your inbox and how much time you’re willing to commit to do so is essential for fighting overload.
How you spend your time defines who you are as a leader. Never confuse a required activity for productivity.
